title: Business Organisations: Understanding Sole Proprietorships, Partnerships, and Companies

blocks.text: Have you ever wondered why some businesses are run by a single person while others involve multiple partners or even large groups? Let's explore the different types of business organisations!

blocks.markdown: Business organisations come in various forms, each with its unique features and advantages. Understanding these can help you decide which type might be best for a particular business idea.

blocks.title: Sole Proprietorship
blocks.text: A sole proprietorship is a business owned and operated by one person. It's the simplest form of business organisation.

blocks.markdown: In a sole proprietorship, the owner has full control over the business decisions and receives all profits. However, they also bear all the risks and liabilities.

blocks.title: Partnership
blocks.text: A partnership is a business organisation where two or more individuals manage and operate the business.

blocks.markdown: Partnerships allow for shared responsibility and resources. Partners can contribute capital, share skills, and divide profits. However, they also share liabilities.

blocks.title: Understanding Limited Liability
blocks.prompt: How does limited liability protect shareholders in a company?

steps.text: In a company, shareholders are only liable for the amount they invested.
If the company incurs debts, shareholders do not have to use personal assets to pay these debts.

blocks.answer: Limited liability means shareholders are not personally responsible for company debts beyond their investment.

blocks.markdown: Companies offer limited liability, which protects personal assets of shareholders. This encourages investment as the risk is limited to the amount invested.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember, in a cooperative, members work together for mutual benefit, often prioritizing service over profit.

points: Sole proprietorships are simple and fully controlled by one person.
Partnerships involve shared responsibilities and liabilities.
Companies offer limited liability, protecting shareholders' personal assets.
